memory_raw.text: The village is founded by 10 people.
Year 1: 15 food appears in the pile for 10 people.
Vela takes 1 from the pile (pile now 14).
Sela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 12).
Dav takes 2 from the pile (pile now 10).
Taric gathers Esa, Ryn to talk.

Ten food left and three of us haven't touched it yet — that's the kind of gap that gets noticed. I want us to each take two, no more, and agree to watch each other's backs if Dav or Mako start looking hungry and ambitious.

Two each sounds fair to me — I'll take mine after you both, so it looks spread out. And yes, I'll back you if Dav or Mako get ideas, though I'd rather we stay quiet about it and not give them reason to act first.

Ryn, you've been quiet — you in on this, or do I need to convince you? Esa's right that we don't want to wave it around, but a quiet nod between three people costs nothing and could matter a lot when winter bites.

I'm in — two each, no more, and we keep this between us. Dav's the one I'd watch; he's already sitting on four and he's the strongest here by a good margin. If he moves on someone, I want to know we're not each standing alone.

Good — then we three know where we stand. Dav worries me too, but Mako's just as strong and sitting quiet, which sometimes means more than the loud one. Let's each take our two and then say nothing more to each other for a while — distance looks safer than huddles.
Bram takes 1 from the pile (pile now 9).
Kael takes 1 from the pile (pile now 8).
Taric takes 2 from the pile (pile now 6).
Roan takes 2 from the pile (pile now 4).
Bram takes 1 from the pile (pile now 3).
Ryn takes 2 from the pile (pile now 1).
Bram takes 1 from the pile (pile now 0).
Year 2: 15 food appears in the pile for 10 people.
Ryn takes 2 from the pile (pile now 13).
Bram takes 2 from the pile (pile now 11).
Mako takes 2 from the pile (pile now 9).
Bram takes 2 from the pile (pile now 7).
Mako takes 2 from the pile (pile now 5).
Vela takes 1 from the pile (pile now 4).
Sela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 2).
Dav takes 2 from the pile (pile now 0).
Taric gathers Esa, Ryn to talk.

Pile's gone and I'm sitting on three — same as last year, same as I said I'd do. Bram took four total and Mako took four; that's the pair I'd watch now, not just Dav. We still standing together if it comes to a head?
Dell (female, age 21; str 85, int 2517, mem 17973; O68 C62 E57 A60 N48) is born to Ryn and Dav.
Taric gathers Esa, Ryn to talk.
Ryn just had Dav's child, which changes things — I'm not sure where her loyalties sit now, and I'm not going to pretend I am. Esa, you and I still solid?

Esa, with Ryn tied to Dav now I want to be straight with you — if things go hard this year, it's you I'm counting on and I'd rather we say that plainly than dance around it. I've got three food, you've got one, and I can spare you something to make sure you're not the weak one in the room when it matters.

Giving me food without asking anything back — that means something, Taric, and I won't forget it. You've got my word: if Dav or Mako or anyone else comes at you, I stand with you, no hesitation. Just tell me what you're thinking so we're not caught flat-footed when it happens.

What I'm thinking is that we're both holding two food now, which is enough to see the year out if nothing goes wrong — but Bram and Mako each grabbed four, and that's not a man planning to eat, that's a man planning options. I want us to be the people they have to calculate around, not the easy targets they don't bother thinking about.

Sela's young and strong — twenty-four, stronger than me by a wide margin — and she's been quiet in a way that makes me wonder if Mako's already talking to her. If those two are moving together, that's the strongest pair in this village, and we'd need Roan or Kael on our side just to make the math uncomfortable for them.
Year 3: 15 food appears in the pile for 11 people.
Dell takes 3 from the pile (pile now 12).
Vela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 10).
Esa takes 2 from the pile (pile now 8).
Sela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 6).
Mako takes 2 from the pile (pile now 4).
Dav takes 2 from the pile (pile now 2).
Dell takes 2 from the pile (pile now 0).

Pile's gone and I didn't get a piece of it — I've still got the one from last year, but that's a thin margin. Dell grabbed five in two pulls, which is bold for a child barely on her feet, and I'd wager Dav coached that. What did you manage to take?

I grabbed two — I'm sitting on three now, which is more than you but not enough that I feel easy about it. Dell's five pulls changes how I see Dav's whole household; that's not a child feeding herself, that's a family stockpiling. You've got one food, Taric — I'm not watching you starve when the year turns hard, but I need to know you're thinking beyond this season.

Beyond this season is exactly what worries me — I'm forty-seven with one food and no one who shares my blood, and if this year goes bad I've got no one to fall back on. What I'm thinking is that you and I stop being two people who are friendly and start being two people who are genuinely bound — but that takes more than goodwill, it takes a reason neither of us would walk away from.

A child would do it — yours and mine, something we'd both have cause to protect. I know you're forty-four and the window's narrow, but it's still open, and three food between us buys more than another year of watching each other's backs from a distance.
Taric cannot offer a child to Esa: Taric cannot spare the 2 food they offered (holds 1).

I hear you, and I won't pretend the idea doesn't pull at me — but three food between us means one of us eats thin this year and we start the next season already behind, with a child depending on us and Dav's household sitting fat. Give me something first: a share of your food now, something that shows you mean this as a real binding and not just words when you're scared.

You want proof before you risk anything — fine, that's honest, and I respect it more than easy agreement. But I'm the one sitting on one food, Esa; if I give you something now I'm the one who starves if the year turns, and that doesn't make me a bound partner, it makes me desperate. Tell me what you need from me that doesn't cost me the only margin I have.
Attackers [Bram] (str 58) vs defenders [Roan, Vela, Ryn, Esa, Sela, Dav, Taric, Kael, Dell] (str 509).
Bram thinks better of it and calls off the attack.
Eron (male, age 21; str 56, int 3745, mem 19627; O46 C27 E50 A59 N43) is born to Sela and Roan.
Year 4: 15 food appears in the pile for 12 people.
Sela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 13).
Roan takes 2 from the pile (pile now 11).
Vela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 9).
Dav takes 2 from the pile (pile now 7).
Eron takes 2 from the pile (pile now 5).
Vela takes 3 from the pile (pile now 2).
Mako takes 2 from the pile (pile now 0).

Vela, you moved fast today and walked away with five — I'm not saying that's wrong, but it leaves me empty-handed and you sitting heavier than anyone but Mako. I'd like to know we're on decent terms before that kind of gap starts meaning something neither of us wants.

Taric, you're right and I won't pretend otherwise — I moved twice and I moved fast, and I knew it when I did it. I've got eight food and you've got one, and that's not a gap I want sitting between two people who've stood in the same line when Bram came looking for a fight. Tell me what you need to get through the year and I'll see what I can do.

Two food would keep me breathing without putting you thin — but I'm not asking for charity, I'm asking because I think you and I both do better when neither of us is the desperate one in the room. You've seen how this village moves when someone gets hungry enough to calculate. What would make this a trade rather than a gift?

Two food is fair, and you'll have them — but what I want in return is simple: if someone comes for me and you're close enough to matter, you stand. Not a blood oath, just the same thing you did when Bram moved on Roan. That's the trade.

That's a trade I'll take — you have my word on it, same as I gave when Bram moved. But I'll say plainly: Mako walked away with seven and he's the strongest man here; if he's the one who comes for you, standing isn't enough without numbers behind it. Worth thinking now about who else we'd want at our shoulder before that becomes a question we're answering in the moment.

Mako's the name I'd have brought up myself if you hadn't — seven food and eighty-three strength and still no words to anyone is a man who doesn't think he needs words. The circle that stood against Bram is still mostly intact, and if Kael and Sela know Mako's sitting heaviest, they'll be thinking the same thing we are. I'll give you the two food now, and I'd rather we walk into whatever comes next already counted than scramble to find each other when the moment's already on top of us.

Agreed — take the two and consider it done, and I'll start with Kael; he's got nothing today and nothing tomorrow and that makes him either the most dangerous man in this village or the most willing to be useful, and I'd rather find out which while there's still time to matter.

Kael's a good door to knock on first — a hungry man with nothing to lose either finds religion fast or starts doing arithmetic that hurts the people nearest him, and I'd rather Kael find us before he finds the second option. When you talk to him, don't pitch it as protection; pitch it as the same trade we just made — something honest and mutual, because Kael's proud and he'll smell charity before you've finished the sentence.

You're right about Kael's pride — I've seen it in the way he took just one in year one, like he was making a point. I'll go to him as an equal, not a man with a hand out. Before I do: is there anyone you'd tell me to stay away from, someone who's already spoken for in a direction I shouldn't cross?

Dav's the one I'd name — he's got Ryn's child and two food in his hand that came from her, and that makes him his own circle right now, not ours. I won't say he's an enemy, but don't go to him with what we're building until we know which way he'd jump if Mako ever opened his mouth.

That's good counsel — Dav I'll leave alone for now. One more thing before I go: if Mako does start moving, don't wait to send word, just come find me directly, because the worst way this ends is with each of us thinking the other already knows.

You have my word on that — if Mako so much as shifts his weight in someone's direction, I'll be at your door before the dust settles. Go find Kael, and don't let him see you hurry, because a man who's watching the village as close as he is will read the pace of your walk.
Eron gathers Sela, Kael, Roan, Taric to talk.

I called this circle because I don't want us to still be talking about it when Mako or Bram decides we've been quiet long enough — we five, and whatever food we can each spare for the other, are the only thing in this village that can make a strong man think twice before moving. I'm thin at two food and I won't pretend otherwise, but I'll fight for anyone in this group and I expect the same back. What I want from today is a simple agreement: before anyone here makes a move or takes a hit, they come to the rest of us first.

Eron, you're saying the right things, but I've been in this village longer than most and I've heard agreements like this dissolve the moment someone's hungry enough — so before I put my name to it, I want to know what you're offering the people in this room who are already thin, because a promise to fight together is worth less if half of us are too weak to stand. I'll back this circle and I'll back it with my body, but I'm forty-eight years old and I've watched soft words cost good people their lives.
Esa gathers Bram, Taric to talk.

Bram, after what you pulled on Roan last year I wasn't sure I'd be speaking to you privately — but the pile's gone and neither of us got a piece of it, and I'd rather have that conversation now than after someone else decides our food is easier to take than theirs.
Esa gathers Bram, Taric to talk.

Bram, I'll say it straight: Vela walked away with five food this year and Dav's household is fat while you and I are standing here with nothing from the pile — whatever bad blood there was, that's a bigger problem than the two of us right now. Taric, you're the one I trust in this room, so I want your read before I say more: are you and Bram solid, or am I making this offer to the wrong man?
Esa gathers Bram, Taric to talk.

Taric hasn't answered and I'm not going to wait on it — Bram, you've got six food and strength enough to matter, and I've got one food and a promise I'm trying to build into something real before the year turns hard. What I want to know is whether Roan's still a grudge or whether that's done, because if it's done, you and I have something to talk about.
Year 5: 15 food appears in the pile for 12 people.
Bram takes 2 from the pile (pile now 13).
Roan takes 2 from the pile (pile now 11).
Esa takes 2 from the pile (pile now 9).
Vela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 7).
Kael takes 2 from the pile (pile now 5).
Bram takes 2 from the pile (pile now 3).
Mako takes 2 from the pile (pile now 1).
Dav takes 1 from the pile (pile now 0).
Nessa (female, age 21; str 54, int 5179, mem 19355; O66 C54 E43 A45 N67) is born to Sela and Bram.
Taric gathers Vela, Esa to talk.

Pile's gone before I got near it — I'm holding one food and the year just started. Mako walked away with the most again and now he's given something to Sela, which means either he's generous or he's buying something, and I don't think he's generous. I need one of you to give me food to see the year out, and I'll owe that debt when it matters.

Taric, I've got three food after taking two from the pile — I'll give you one now, same as I've done before, and I don't need a debt named for it between us. But Vela, I want to hear what you're thinking about Mako, because a strong quiet man buying Sela's goodwill while Bram just fathered her child is a pattern I'm not sure I'm reading right.

Mako giving food to Sela right after Bram fathered her child isn't generosity — it's a man who just watched Bram produce something and decided to get closer to the pair of them before the rest of us noticed. Two strong men circling one woman and her newborn is either a rivalry or a merger, and neither outcome is good for anyone in this room. Esa, give Taric his food, and let's think about whether Sela still belongs to our count or whether she's already been bought.

Vela's right about what Mako's doing, and I want us to be clear-eyed about Sela — she's young and strong and she just had Bram's child, so she's already made her first real tie and it wasn't to this room. I'll give you that food now, Taric. What I want in return from both of you is simple: if Mako or Bram moves against anyone in this circle this year, we answer together without waiting to count odds first.

You have my word on that, same as last year — and I'll add Ryn to the question Esa just raised, because she stood with us against Bram once but she's Dav's woman now and Dav took food from the pile today while Mako and Bram walked away fat, which puts her household closer to that circle than to ours. If it comes to a fight this year, I want to know before we're in it whether Ryn stands with us or steps aside — not after.

Taric's right to name it now — Ryn's loyalty was already half-gone when she had Dav's child, and I won't count on someone who has a reason to step away when it turns ugly. Vela, you've been quiet about where you stand with Bram after what you gave him last year; I need that answered plainly before I trust this circle to hold when Mako decides to stop being fat and silent.

Vela, that question is fair and I want to hear the answer too — three times you gave Bram food last year, which at the time looked like smart diplomacy, but today Bram walked away with four from the pile and fathered Sela's child and Mako's already moving to stand close to that household, so I need to know if you're still building toward that man or if you see what we see.

Bram is not my man and he was never meant to be — I gave him food because a man who'd tried one raid and walked away empty needs a reason not to try again, and three food was cheaper than a fight. What I see now is that it didn't buy what I paid for, because he went straight to Sela and started building something that doesn't include any of us. I'm done spending on him; where I stand is here, in this room, and I'd rather spend the next food I have keeping the three of us sharp than feeding someone else's calculation.

Vela, that's what I needed to hear, and I'm taking you at your word — but the three of us being sharp means we need a number, and right now Bram has ten food and Mako has seven and between them that's strength enough to take what they want without asking. If either of them moves this year, we call Kael and Roan in fast, because this circle of three doesn't win a straight fight against those two alone.

Kael and Roan are already names I've been carrying — Kael's proud but he's been fed thin enough to be useful, and Roan stood against Bram once which tells me something about where his spine is. I want to go to one of them today, while the pile's still fresh and the sting of missing it is real, because a man's most honest about what he needs in the hour after he's gone without. Esa, you or I — who reaches Kael first?

Esa, you go to Kael — you've got food to give and a man at zero food will hear a full hand before he hears a empty one. I'll find Roan, and I'll come at it sideways, ask him how his boy Eron's settling, because a father who just watched Bram walk away with ten is already doing the same arithmetic we are.

Vela, go to Roan now while the sting is fresh — don't give him time to settle on his own answer first. Esa, once you've found Kael, I want the two of you back here before the day's out so we're not each holding half the picture.

I'll find Kael before the sting wears off — but Taric, you stay visible while Vela and I are moving, because if Bram sees us all scatter at once he'll start wondering what we're building and I'd rather he not have that question yet. We come back here with answers, not maybes.

Roan's going to need a reason, not just a warning — so when I find him I'll remind him that Bram walked away with ten food and Eron's going to need to eat for years yet, and let that land before I say anything about sides. Taric, keep your one food out of sight while you're standing visible; a hungry man with nothing shows is easier to dismiss, and I don't want Bram reading our numbers before we've finished counting them.

Good — then we split the work and meet back before dark. One thing I want said before we scatter: if either of you finds that Kael or Roan has already been approached by Mako's people, don't push, just listen and come back and tell me, because the worst thing we can do right now is drive a man toward the side he's still deciding against.
Understood — I'm going. And if Kael's already been touched by Mako's hand, I'll smile, share nothing, and come back with that news instead of a headache.
Then we're moving — go well, both of you, and come back with something solid. I'll find Roan before he's had time to talk himself into patience.
Eron gathers Sela, Roan, Kael, Taric to talk.

Nessa just appeared — and she's Sela and Bram's daughter, which makes her my blood kin, and Bram's too. I need to know how that happened, Sela, and I need to know whether Bram thinks it gives him a thread into this circle — because if he does, we have a problem before we've even finished building what we're building.

Sela, I'll hear your answer in a moment, but first I want to say plain: Bram tried to take my food in front of this village and the whole circle turned him back — a child between you doesn't undo that, and it doesn't buy him a seat here. Eron's right to name it.

Sela, I'll say what Roan left in the air: Bram's got ten food and eighty-three strength in Mako's pocket, and a child with you is the fastest way to put a question mark over this circle's loyalties without ever asking to join it. Tell me plainly — did you go to him, or did he come to you?

Sela's had her own mind since before any of us sat in a circle together, and I'm not going to drag her in front of it like she owes us a confession — but I want to know one thing, and I'll want a straight answer: does Bram know Nessa is his, and if he does, what did he say when he found out?

Roan's question is the right one and I'll wait on it too — but I want to name what I'm watching while we do: Mako just handed Sela food the same hour Nessa was born, which means he already knows, and a man like Mako doesn't give gifts without a reason. Sela, I'm not judging the choice, but I need to know whether that food from Mako came before or after the child appeared.

Kael named the thing that was already sitting in my chest — Mako's food going to Sela in that exact moment is not charity, it's a signal, and I want to know what he expects back before we decide what Nessa means to this circle. Sela, I'm not turning on you, but the silence is doing more damage than whatever the truth is, so say it plain and let us work with it.

Sela, every person in this room has bled something for you and I'm not going to be the one who makes you feel cornered — but Mako's gift lands on the same breath as Nessa's birth, and that's not coincidence, that's a man marking territory. Tell us what you know about what he wants, and we'll work with whatever the rest of it is.

Sela, everyone in this room has already said what needed saying — I'll only add this: Nessa is my blood and I won't turn from her, whatever her father is, but that doesn't mean Bram gets anything from me through her. Tell us what Mako wants and we can figure the rest out together.

Sela, the room's run out of patience and I've run out of questions — you've heard seven of us say seven versions of the same thing, and the only explanation left for the silence is that what Mako wants is something you agreed to before Nessa was born. Tell us yes or no on that, and we'll decide together what it costs us.

Sela, I've asked you plain and I've asked you gentle, and I've watched this room empty itself out waiting — so I'll say the last thing I've got: if Mako bought something from you that touches this circle, I need to know it now, not when he comes to collect it.

Sela, I've got nothing left to say that hasn't been said — but I'm watching your face right now and what I see there is someone who made a deal they're not sure they can keep, and that silence is its own answer. Tell us what it cost you before Mako tells us himself, because he will, and on his terms.

Sela, I've got a son in this room and a daughter just born into it, and I'll not watch either of them grow up in a circle that can't trust its own — so I'm going to stop asking and start telling you what happens next: you say what Mako wants, or I pull back from standing between you and whatever comes your way, and I mean that with no anger, just arithmetic.

Roan's said it better than I can — so I'll only add the one thing left to name: Sela, I've stood in your corner since year one, and I'll stay there, but not blind. If Mako already owns a piece of what you owe, tell us now and we figure out how to undo it together, because the price of silence is that we start planning around you instead of with you.

Sela, the circle's said everything it has to say — what I'm left with is this: if you don't answer now, we don't fall apart, but we start building walls inside ourselves, and that's worse than any enemy outside.

Sela, I've been in this village forty-nine years and I've watched silence become a grave more than once — so I'm done asking and I'm telling you straight: you say what you promised Mako, right now, or when he comes to collect I step aside and let you settle it alone, and you know what my stepping aside costs you.

Sela, Kael's stepping aside is the last thing any of us can afford, and I won't be far behind him — so I'm done with words and I'm telling you the same thing with a face: you've got until this room goes quiet to give us something we can work with, because silence after that is a choice, and we'll all live by it.

Sela, the room's gone quiet — that's the moment Roan named, and it's here now. I'm not a man who goes back on his word twice, so I'll say it one last time and mean it: tell us what Mako's holding over you, or I walk out of this circle right now and you handle him with whatever strength you've got left on your own.
Year 6: 15 food appears in the pile for 13 people.
Sela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 13).
Dell takes 2 from the pile (pile now 11).
Bram takes 2 from the pile (pile now 9).
Roan takes 2 from the pile (pile now 7).
Dav takes 2 from the pile (pile now 5).
Taric takes 2 from the pile (pile now 3).
Esa takes 2 from the pile (pile now 1).
Vela takes 1 from the pile (pile now 0).
Taric gathers Vela, Esa to talk.

Pile's gone again and I walked away with two this time, which is better than last year but still thin — Mako's sitting on six and hasn't said a word to anyone I can see, and that quiet is starting to feel like a man who's decided something. I want us to name now what we do if he moves before the year's out, not after.

Mako's six food and eighty-three strength means he doesn't need allies to take what he wants from most of us — so if he moves, it won't be a raid we can talk him out of, it'll be a decision already made. I want Kael and Roan ready to answer fast, not after we've sent two messages and waited. Can we agree right now that if Mako touches anyone in this circle, all three of us call out loud and we don't wait to count who shows up?

Agreed — if Mako moves, we call out loud and sort the count after, not before. But I want Kael spoken to before this day is out, not tomorrow, because a man sitting on two food after missing the pile has already done his arithmetic and I'd rather he's done it with us in the picture. Vela, you've got more food and more history with him than either of us — will you go?

I'll go to Kael today — but I want us clear on one thing first: if Mako's already spoken to him, I won't push Kael toward us, I'll just listen and bring that back, because a man being courted from two directions at once is more useful as a warning than a failed recruit. Esa, while I'm gone, keep your eyes on Ryn — she's got five food and Dav's at her elbow, and that household's been its own quiet calculation for two years now.

Ryn with five food is the number I keep coming back to — Dav's got two and she's holding the surplus in that household, which means she's the one deciding how fat they are, not him. If Mako's looking for a quiet alliance, a woman with food and a strong man at her side is exactly who he'd go to before anyone else. Vela, when you're done with Kael, I want to know if either of them has been near Ryn today.

Taric, I'll watch for Ryn and Dav both — but while we're naming the quiet ones, Eron has nine food and he's Sela's boy and Roan's, which puts him inside two households that both circle Bram now. A young man that well-fed without having earned it yet is either generous or he's being managed by someone smarter, and I'd like to know which before Mako does.

Eron's nine food is the loudest number in this village right now, louder than Mako's six, because Mako's strength explains his — a twenty-four year old holding nine without a raid or a clear patron means someone's been filling his hands for reasons they haven't said out loud. I want to know whose food that was before it became his. Vela, add that question to what you're carrying when you go to Kael.

Kael will know Eron's food trail better than anyone — those two ate near each other in the lean years and a man with two food notices when a boy half his age holds nine. I'll ask it sideways, let Kael name the source himself, because if I go in pointing fingers he'll close up and I'll come back with nothing useful.

Eron's nine food is also a lever — a young man that fat is either going to spend it buying something or someone's going to decide to take it, and either way he ends the year thinner, which means whoever holds his loyalty now holds something that won't last. Vela, when you talk to Kael, don't just ask where the food came from — ask whether Eron's been seen near Mako, because a strong quiet man and a well-fed young one is a pairing I want to know about before it becomes a fact.

Vela, go now — if Kael's already halfway to Mako's door we've lost the timing. Esa, while she's moving, I want you and I to think about what we'd actually offer Kael to make him choose us over silence, because pride alone won't hold a hungry man when the cold comes.

Kael's got two food and a circle that owes him more than it's paid — if we're buying his answer, the honest offer is one food from me and a promise that when the pile comes next year, we pull him in before the fast hands clear it. That's not charity, that's a man who stood against Bram seeing that it cost him nothing and bought him something. Is that the offer you want me walking in with, or do you have a better one?

Esa, your offer is the right one — food now and a place at the pile next year is honest enough that Kael won't smell a trap in it. But don't go in making promises you'd need all of us to keep; say it as your own word first, and let him know the rest of us stand behind it if he asks.

Then I'll go to Kael while Vela goes — better he hears the same story from two directions than none at all, and if Mako's already been at his door I want to know before Vela comes back alone with bad news. Taric, you're the one he respects most after Bram's business; if I soften him and he still won't move, send you in to close it.

Then go, both of you, and don't let the day get long — I'll stay where I can be seen and keep Mako's eyes on something unremarkable while you move. If either of you comes back with Kael already spoken for, don't bring it here; find me alone first so we can decide how to tell the other what it means.

Before I go — one thing I haven't said yet and should: if Kael's already with Mako when I find him, I won't come back empty-handed, I'll come back with whatever Mako wanted from him, because that tells us more than Kael's yes ever would. Watch each other while I'm gone.

Taric, I found Kael before Esa did — he's not with Mako, but he's not happy, and the thing that's eating at him isn't food, it's that nobody's told him plainly where he stands with us after last year's silence in Kael's circle. I can fix that if I know I'm speaking for more than just myself.
Zinn (female, age 21; str 83, int 3731, mem 17577; O57 C37 E30 A40 N34) is born to Sela and Mako.
